[3:38PM] #VI #TrafficUpdate 

Traffic movement from McWen Bridge inward Bonny Camp Roundabout is currently flowing smoothly. Similarly, the route inward Ahmadu Bello Way is largely free, with only a slight delay observed at the Adeola Odeku junction due to ongoing alternation delays. The return journey back to Bonny Camp also remains relatively clear.

Vehicular flow along Adetokunbo Ademola, heading toward the Eko Hotel Roundabout, is steady. However, traffic is beginning to build up near the roundabout due to the closing hour rush and traffic alternations at that point. Movement from Eko Hotel toward Sanusi Fafunwa is steady and progressing.

From Bonny Camp underbridge enroute Kofo Abayomi, vehicular movement is good. Kofo Abayomi inbound to Oniru is busy but moving, affected by the closing hour rush and traffic alternations.

Traffic from the Law School axis enroute Civic Centre is experiencing a high influx of vehicles but remains in motion. From Civic Centre toward BJ1004, there is a steady flow of vehicles around the BJ1004 area. Once past BJ1004, traffic improves considerably along the route to School Corner, Sandfield, and into Lekki Phase 1.

The return journey from Lekki through Sandfield, connecting School Corner, is smooth. BJ1004 inbound Civic Centre experiences moving traffic.

Traffic from Civic Centre to the Ramp bridge is gradually building up, while the movement toward Law School connecting Akin Adesola is encouraging. Akin Adesola toward Kilimanjaro is also experiencing steady traffic flow.

Movement from Kilimanjaro to Kofo and onward to Bonny Camp Roundabout is slightly busy but remains in motion, with some delays due to road alternation works underneath Bonny Camp Bridge.

Overall, only slight traffic delays are being experienced at known alternation points, and no impediments have been sighted at this time.

#FollowLASTMA

GCV Army: Guardians of a Vision, Defenders of Our Community

In every movement, there comes a moment when silence is no longer an option when the future of a vision rests in the hands of those brave enough to fight for it. That moment came, and the GCV Army answered.

The GCV Army is not a metaphor it is a living, breathing force. It is the frontline of our defense, the engine of our expansion, and the soul of our evolution. Composed of fearless Pioneers across the nation, this force stands as a shield against misinformation, doubt, and division. In the Philippines, that shield is held firm by 21 extraordinary individuals the GCV Fleet Admirals.

These Admirals are not just commanders. They are protectors of our merchants, defenders of our values, and torchbearers of our mission. Amid the storms of skepticism and the noise of resistance, they remained steadfast. Not for applause but for belief. Not for praise but for purpose. 
 
This video is not simply a tribute. It is a declaration.

We honor the heart of the GCV Army their mission, their sacrifice, and the unbreakable spirit of the 21 Fleet Admirals who lead with courage and serve with soul. It is also a rallying cry to expand, to strengthen, and to ignite this force across every province of the Philippines and beyond its shores. 

The GCV Army is made of volunteers but not ordinary ones. These are individuals who believe in a decentralized, people-powered economy grounded in trust, transparency, and technology. And unlike traditional armies, the GCV Army does not bear weapons it bears wisdom, truth, and action.

Their mission is clear: 

To educate the public about GCV and the Pi Network.

To protect the ecosystem from misinformation and manipulation. 
 
To respond to digital attacks that aim to divide or demoralize the community.

Where others scroll, they speak. Where others watch, they act. Where others give up, they rise again. 

What separates the GCV Army from any other force is not just its strategy, but its soul. These warriors are not funded. They are not ordered. They are called and they answer with their hearts.

In the face of confusion and hate, they respond with clarity and compassion. When doubt spreads, they speak hope. When tension rises, they bring calm.

They have shown: 
Resilience in the face of relentless backlash  
Empathy in guiding both allies and skeptics 
Calm leadership in volatile, emotional climates  
 
To believe in something that the world hasn’t yet embraced takes a different kind of faith. The kind that holds light when everything around you goes dark. That is what each GCV Fleet Admiral embodies. That is why the movement remains unshaken.

Today, we stand on sacred ground. What we do next will echo in the years to come. When the world asks: What kept the GCV mission alive during the darkest hours? We will answer: “The army of believers who refused to give up.”    

To our 21 Fleet Admirals you are not just defenders of an ecosystem. You are builders of a new future.

You are protecting our community’s spirit.

You are proving that ordinary people can do 
extraordinary things when purpose leads the way.
Your courage is contagious.

Your leadership is irreplaceable.

Your loyalty is priceless.

The world is watching.

The mission continues.

And because of you it grows stronger every day.

Onward, warriors. The vision lives because you do.

“The 21 Stand”
For the GCV Fleet Admirals of the Philippines
They stood when the winds began to howl,
Unmoved by fear, with heads held proud.
Twenty-one voices, one unshaken vow 
To guard the dream, to not back down.

In silence, they marched where truth called loud,
Not for glory, not for a crowd.
But for freedom’s fire, for justice near,
For every soul they hold dear.

Their names may not echo in the halls of kings,
But their courage moves the deepest things.
With hearts of steel and eyes that see,
Against the storm, against the night,
They lit the path, became the light.

For GCV, for kin and land,
The future rose—because they stand.
Oh Fleet Admirals, fierce and true, 
The shield, the voice, the honored line,
Guardians of a cause divine.

So today we sing, with pride and grace,
Your spirit time cannot erase.
The 21 who took the call—
You are our heroes. You gave your all.

With deepest respect,
Ms. Lumari
Executive Director & Committee Chair
Global GCV Core Team

401 BRIDGE TRAFFIC ADVISORY FROM FDOT Central Florida:  

S.R. 401 Eastern Bridge in Brevard County Set to Close Tonight 

Motorists are advised that the eastern movable bridge that connects westbound State Road (S.R.) 528 to northbound S.R. 401 will be closed continuously beginning as early as Wednesday, July 9. This closure is expected to remain in place through September 2025.

Motorists traveling westbound on S.R. 528 who wish to access northbound S.R. 401 should follow signage to the middle bridge, which will revert to regular northbound traffic after crossing.

Southbound S.R. 401 traffic from the middle bridge will remain shifted to the western bridge. Therefore, motorists traveling southbound on S.R. 401 who wish to access eastbound S.R. 528 should follow signage to the westernmost bridge and then use the access road on the east side to reach the eastbound S.R. 528 on ramp.

Please see attached map for detour information. The work schedule is subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances. For more details, please visit https://t.co/58XPk0hGMr

FDOT encourages motorists to use caution, remain alert, and follow posted detour signs through the work zone.

@MyFDOT
